note: SC 2026 US Senate SPECIAL primary (Aug 11, runoff Aug 25). REPUBLICAN ONLY — and that is a statutory fact, not a coverage gap. The contest is held under S.C. Code §7-11-55 after the death of the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate; because that nominee had general-election opposition, the special filing period was open to REPUBLICAN candidates only, and voters who cast a ballot in the June Democratic primary are barred from the August 11 contest. The winner goes onto the November 3 general ballot in the deceased nominee's place. Sources: the SC Election Commission notice (2026-07-13), concurring county-board notices, and the LWV state guide; independently corroborated by Ballotpedia, which links an August 11 REPUBLICAN primary page and no Democratic counterpart. Verified 2026-08-05 (HO 600). DO NOT re-add a `-special-D` entry from the symmetry of the R one: a §7-11-55 special primary is single-party BY CONSTRUCTION whenever the deceased nominee had general-election opposition. HO 600 deleted the live phantom D row (scripts/delete-sc-special-d-600.ts) and removed its seed entry in the same commit — both halves are required, because this loader is a pure INSERT ... ON CONFLICT with no delete pass, so a seed entry alone recreates the row and a delete alone gets undone by the next seed run. ROSTER: empty on purpose. Ballotpedia HAS published the field since candidate filing closed 2026-07-28 — 10 Republicans, at https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_South_Carolina,_2026_(August_11_Republican_primary) — but no automated path reaches it yet: senateSpecialPageUrl builds the `United_States_Senate_special_election_in_{Slug},_2026` shape, which 404s for SC (that shape is Ballotpedia's convention for a special *election*, i.e. FL/OH; SC's August 11 contest is a special *primary* for the regular Class-2 seat and lives as a parenthetical page on the regular race page), and even given the right URL parseCandidatesPage DROPS the box, because isSpecialElectionPage() keys on the page <title> and the parenthetical title carries no 'special election' string while the votebox <h5> reads 'Special Republican primary' — so the page-type gate inverts against itself. Both are measured, not inferred (HO 600 M3/M4). The roster must be SOURCED when that is fixed, never invented. An empty `candidates` array asserts nothing and leaves any later-filled roster untouched (HO 560 amend). The June rows (senate-SC-2026-{D,R}) are a different id set, settled with recorded shares, untouched by this seed.
